summary: The change enables the covered anonymous-shape cases and the frontend tests pass, but two valid literals produce the wrong value after Go emission. Both failures come from evaluating or copying properties at a different point than JavaScript does.

findings.claim: When an inferred literal reuses a named shape, property initializers are left in constructor order rather than source order. The tempInit guard only covers shape.* classes, so side effects can be reversed even though the HIR verifies and emits.
findings.repro: Input: type Row={a:number;b:number}; export class Probe { static count=0; static next():number{this.count++;return this.count} static take(x:Row):number{return x.b*10+x.a} static run():number{const value={b:this.next(),a:this.next()};return this.take(value)} } . Lower and Go-emit Probe.run(): it returns 21; JavaScript returns 12.

findings.claim: A spread saves the source reference but delays reading its fields until constructor argument evaluation. A later property initializer can mutate that source, so the constructed anonymous object contains the new value instead of the value at the spread position.
findings.repro: Input: export class Probe { static src={a:1,b:2}; static touch():number{const x=this.src;x.b=7;return 0} static run():number{const obj={...this.src,c:this.touch()};return obj.b} } . Lower and Go-emit Probe.run(): it returns 7; JavaScript returns 2.
